claim: Every preprocessor page says `minimum_version: "v47"` and 'Available in PNut/pnut_ts v47 and later compilers' (oneliners '(v47+)'). The v55 change log says the pre-processor was added in v48 (2025-01-06): '#DEFINE, #UNDEF, #IFDEF, #IFNDEF, #ELSEIFDEF, #ELSEIFNDEF, #ELSE, #ENDIF', with -D on the command line. preprocessor-overview.yaml contradicts itself: :304 'Available in v47+ compilers' against :308 'External symbols can be defined via command line with -D option (v48+)'. (#ERROR/#WARN/#INCLUDE/#PRAGMA are PNut-TS extensions that have no PNut version.)

`gps_weight := sensor_weights[GPS_SENSOR] * 0.3` and `baro_weight := sensor_weights[BARO_SENSOR] * 0.7` multiply an integer by a float literal with the integer `*`. Float literals are IEEE-754 bit patterns; weighting needs `*.` on float values (or integer scaling such as `* 3 / 10`). The block compiles, so the gate cannot see it (and this block is red for other, registered reasons).
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/spin2-v55/spin2-v55-text.txt:346 ('Special floating-point operators (+. -. *. /.) treat long values as floats'), :455 (`*.` Floating-point multiply)

claim: setup_board_clocking calls `clkset(CRYSTAL_FREQ, CPU_FREQ)` with CRYSTAL_FREQ = 20_000_000 as the first argument. CLKSET's first argument is the new CLKMODE value (the PLL/oscillator configuration word), not the crystal frequency; passing 20_000_000 as a clock mode is meaningless. (The template's other defects are registered: S-088, S-019.)

`address: "512 ($200)"`. $000..$1FF is the cog register space; $200 and up is LUT. v55 gives TASKHLT as a 'Register' (:149) with no address, and the interpreter declares it among its own working registers (`taskhlt res 1`), not at $200. The stated address is outside cog RAM and has no source.

Five examples show what `DEBUG(C_Z)` prints from Spin2 code: after `x := 0` 'Shows: C=0 Z=1 (zero result)', after `x := 1` 'C=0 Z=0', after an inline `org ... end` block 'Shows: C=1 Z=1 (overflow to 0)', 'C=1 means x < y', and notes: 'Reads actual processor flag state at time of DEBUG call'. v55 says only 'Output the C and Z flags as "C=? Z=?". Useful in PASM code.' The flags a DEBUG() statement in Spin2 code reads are the interpreter's working flags at that moment, not the result of the Spin2 assignment or of the preceding inline-PASM block (the interpreter runs between them and `end` leaves the cog executing interpreter code). None of the printed values is sourced or bench-verified. (The three `wc, wz` examples are also registered as a compile defect.)
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/spin2-v55/spin2-v55-text.txt:1006; undetermined here (bench question: DEBUG(C_Z) after x := 0 in Spin2 code)

claim: `long heap[1024]` is 4096 bytes, but alloc adds `heap_ptr` to `@heap` as a BYTE offset and tests `heap_ptr > 1024` as the limit, so the allocator uses 1024 of the 4096 bytes (or, if `size` is meant in longs, advances the pointer a quarter as far as it should). On overflow `heap_ptr` has already advanced, so one failed allocation poisons later ones. The block compiles.
source: the block itself (`long heap[1024]`, `ptr := @heap + heap_ptr`, `if heap_ptr > 1024`)

claim: `target_positions[motor_id] := new_positions[motor_id]` and `current_content[display_id] := content_array[display_id]` index a PARAMETER (`new_positions`, `content_array`) as if it were an array pointer. A parameter is a plain long: `p[i]` indexes the parameter's own storage (the neighbouring stack longs), not the memory it points to; a caller-supplied array needs `long[new_positions][motor_id]`. Both blocks compile.

claim: ORGF is described as 'Set origin address with forced alignment' with the example 'Align to address $100'. ORGF fills with zeros up to the given cog address ('fill to cog address $040 with zeros (no symbol allowed before ORGF)'); it is a fill, and the address is a cog-register address, not an alignment boundary. (The example line is also registered under S-121: `//` comment.)
